Article saves, publication changes (including scheduled publishing), recycle-bin operations, and category/tag updates or deletions invalidate article caches, feeds, and the sitemap. Counters do not trigger invalidation; page-specific sitemap invalidation preserves article/feed caches. Feeds and the sitemap expire after one hour; articles use `PostCacheMinutes`. Invalidation is process-local, so multiple instances require separate coordination. See Caching and Side Effects for implementation details.

Settings become active only after a successful database save; related CDN/avatar settings are saved together. Updates are serialized within one process; other instances must reload or synchronize separately. See the configuration write contract.

The TinyOrmPlayground project is my personal project where I have tested all the TinyORM database queries in the early development phases, currently, it executes ~1600 database queries across the whole TinyORM framework. Every query has a nice title header, is logged to the console, and is counted and measured (elapsed time). Every query also runs on all Supported Databases.

The TinyOrmPlayground project can be compiled in a single-threaded or multi-threaded mode. In the multi-threaded mode, every database connection runs in its own thread. The connection summary is logged at the end of every database connection and the application summary is logged before an exit. Whole TinyOrmPlayground application is configurable through the src/configuration.hpp class.

|**Uniqueness**|Uniqueness functions detect when data constraints are breached like duplicates, number of distinct values etc|
